market_holds: Sealed baseline (2026-11-23 18:08 UTC): spot $6.125, run-up -10.8% over 5 days and -29.4% over 20 days, 66% below the 52-week high, 20-day realised vol 85%. Front straddle 18.8% to 18 Dec; the event-implied move nets out to 5.3% only because ordinary vol is so high. Downside skew is 14.4 vol points, so protection is expensive, yet put/call open interest is only 0.26. The HK line (3896) fell from HK$4.68 on 5 Nov to HK$3.12 on 23 Nov, including -11.5% on 17 Nov (stockanalysis history). The trigger was sector-wide: the BIS interim final rule on remote access to advanced chips (released 16 Nov, effective 19 Nov), Nvidia worries and a Hong Kong AI sell-off. Earnings Whispers puts the fall since the Q2 print at 38.5% (16 Nov), and it reached about -50% from the ~$12 post-Q2 level by today. Consensus has not fallen with the price. Chartmill shows Q3 revenue at RMB3.454bn (+39% y/y, +12.4% q/q on Q2's 3.072bn), revised up 4.7% over three months; EPS is about -$0.04 ADS, whisper -$0.03. There is no formal guide. A July Jiemian report, not confirmed by the company, gives a 2026 revenue target of RMB12.5-13.5bn, which implies H2 of RMB6.7-7.7bn against H1 of 5.78bn; consensus Q3 plus Q4 sits near the middle. Short interest was about 2-3% of float at the end of September (6-8m shares), and I found no November figure. Recent reactions follow modest surprises with large moves: Q2'26 a small revenue beat plus an EPS beat gave +8% to +14% (19 Aug); Q1'26 mixed revenue and an EPS miss gave about -3% to -4%; Q3'25 a revenue miss gave -5% to -8%.
view: This print should turn on whether AI public-cloud capacity converted into revenue in Q3. Demand is not in doubt. Xiaomi's AI compute budget reportedly rose to more than RMB10bn, Alibaba's model team reportedly signed a five-year lease for more than 3,000 eight-GPU servers, and Xiaomi's MiMo models lead third-party token usage. Supply is the gate: management calls chip scarcity 'a new norm', and in H1 fewer than a third of the servers due to Alibaba were delivered. The freshest evidence is from peers that reported the September quarter in the last eight days, and it points to faster Chinese GPU-cloud conversion in Q3. Baidu AI Cloud Infra grew 94% y/y with GPU cloud +43% q/q, Alibaba Cloud accelerated from 45% to 53%, and Tencent cloud grew 35% as compute supply expanded. KC itself spent RMB3.3bn of capex in Q2, which should have come online in Q3; Q1 capex of about RMB2.9bn was followed by a +RMB362m (+18%) q/q jump in public cloud in Q2. Repeating that, with enterprise cloud flat to slightly up on the H2-weighted delivery management described, puts Q3 near RMB3.45-3.55bn: in line to a small beat on a bar that is demanding but not stretched. The price has nearly halved since August on sector and regulatory news while estimates went up. So a clean print with steady margins (Q2 adjusted GM 15.4%, adjusted OPM 4%) plus reassurance that the BIS rule touches a domestic-capacity provider little, or even helps it, could bring a sharp relief move. Against that, KC missed Q3 revenue in both 2024 and 2025 because of enterprise-cloud seasonality. Depreciation and interest are rising, and cash was down to RMB4.67bn against roughly RMB8.8bn of H2 capex, so any financing signal on the call would weigh. The tape is a high-beta China AI tape the morning after a violent sell-off, and Xiaomi reports the same morning. My lean is mildly up, not one I would bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the Q3 acceleration that the peers' September-quarter prints (Baidu GPU cloud +43% q/q, Alibaba Cloud 53%) imply for Chinese GPU-cloud conversion. KC's price fell through those prints because of the BIS rule and Nvidia, so the price does not hold them. Consensus may not either: it was last revised after Q2, and it already demands +12% q/q, so the gap is small and unproven.

recommendation.reason: Peer September-quarter prints and KC's Q2 capex point to strong Q3 AI public-cloud revenue, and the stock has halved on sector and regulatory news while estimates rose. That gives a mild upside lean. But consensus already asks for +12% q/q, KC missed Q3 revenue in each of the last two years, and financing and depreciation risk can dominate the call. The lean is about 56%, below the bar for a recommendation.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue below about RMB3.40bn, or flat-to-down q/q AI gross billings, or the call flagging chip-delivery slippage or a new equity raise or convertible, would make this a down move. Revenue above RMB3.55bn with adjusted GM at 16% or more would make it a clear up move.

self_critique: My upside case rests on peers whose supply chains differ. Baidu and Alibaba run their own chips (Kunlun, T-Head), while KC buys from third parties, and the scarcity Alibaba and Tencent describe could leave KC's deliveries slipping exactly as in H1. Consensus already asks for +12% q/q, and KC has missed Q3 revenue two years running. A capex-heavy, cash-draining story in a tape that punishes AI capex (Tencent's FCF turned negative and the stock still fell) could sell off even on an in-line print, especially if the call hints at financing. Xiaomi reporting the same morning adds noise I cannot read.
approach_notes: P3's stakeholder route paid: peers' September-quarter prints were the freshest evidence on the one line that matters. P4 helped separate a price fall from estimate changes. There is no explicit guide and no reachable consensus history, so 'priced' could only be shown loosely and the edge stayed below P7's bar.
